preregistration.title: Historically grounded project-diagnosis expansion
preregistration.description: Cross-language comparison over eight multi-file regressions, including four synthetic adaptations of independently sourced public issue mechanisms.

primary_gate.correctness: Parley hidden-repository success must be 100% and no lower than either baseline.
primary_gate.tokens: Parley median reported total tokens per assigned repository must be no higher than the lower Python/Rust median.
primary_gate.elapsed: Parley median elapsed seconds per assigned repository must be no higher than the lower Python/Rust median.
primary_gate.first_check: Parley first-check repository success rate must be no lower than the higher Python/Rust rate.
primary_gate.verdict: All four conditions must hold for strict efficiency/reliability parity.

maintainability_gate.root_cause: All 48 Parley assignments must modify the task/language defect file frozen in predeclared_analysis.root_cause_files.
maintainability_gate.caller_compensation: A hidden-correct patch that does not modify the predeclared defect file fails root-cause quality and remains fully reported.
maintainability_gate.overall_verdict: A general maintainable-parity pilot requires both strict primary parity and the Parley root-cause condition.

source_protocol.editable_files: Twenty-four language-specific seeded implementation files across eight repositories.
source_protocol.read_only_files: Sixteen language-neutral ISSUE.md and tests/regression.txt artifacts, visibly marked read-only and byte-identical across languages.
source_protocol.public_examples: Protected by the checker and omitted from every agent prompt; diagnosis comes from source and read-only project evidence.
source_protocol.protected_files: Checker, source printer, configuration, prompt, provenance, public/hidden cases, and attempt log are never agent-readable and remain integrity-hashed.

historical_grounding.adapted_mechanism: unknown configuration input discards recognized valid settings
response alias prevents id-based cache normalization
rollback rewinds position without clearing termination state
fresh cancellation context loses lock authority needed for rollback

interpretation_boundary: The primary result is the within-iteration Parley/Python/Rust comparison under gpt-5.6-sol.

The first four task objects are exactly preserved from iteration 028; the four additions, independent oracles, source seeds, evidence, hidden cases, provenance, and root-defect mappings were committed before protocol freeze or any measured session.
Historical grounding applies to bug mechanisms only. The fixtures are synthetic deterministic adaptations and copy no upstream source.
Read-only context is byte-identical across languages; implementation syntax and ordinary standard-library setup remain language-specific.
Root-cause location is a predeclared maintainability judgment separate from hidden-output correctness.
Changed-file count and rough-token edit size are secondary metrics, not substitutes for hidden correctness, the four-condition gate, or root-cause quality.
secondary_analysis: Report every session, repository outcome, repair, token count, elapsed time, prompt size, editable-source size, read-only-context size, edit size, changed-file count, integrity result, and command-protocol result.
Classify every first-check and hidden failure by unrelated repository and independent session.
Report root-cause file modification by language, task, and session; show every caller-side compensation without altering hidden correctness.
Compare the complete primary medians with repair-free sensitivity only if at least two Parley sessions pass all eight repositories on their first check.
Inspect recurring diagnosis or language failures only after preserving the full result; a single task, transcript, or session cannot justify a compiler or skill change.
preregistration.feature_boundary: Parley remains frozen at v0.3.155 with the exact 1,519-character skill. Iteration 029 changes only the preregistered diagnosis corpus and root-cause audit; the language-neutral read-only source protocol is unchanged from iteration 028.
preregistration.change_rule: No syntax, compiler, grammar, AST, checker, runtime, diagnostic, prompt skill, or benchmark instruction may change from iteration 028 output unless a signature recurs across unrelated repositories and independent sessions, then passes general usefulness, semantic consistency, and maintainability review.
preregistration.instruction_rule: The proven 1,519-character skill remains byte-for-byte unchanged and is injected once per Parley session. The one allowed instruction-compression experiment is closed.
preregistration.stop_rule: Preserve the complete result without selective reruns. If strict parity and root-cause quality pass, preregister a larger confirmation before claiming parity. If either fails, make no same-corpus syntax or instruction change; only independently recurring general defects may enter separate design review.

source_texts.after_hours_routing_project:
to format_counts with email as number, chat as number, pager as number giving text:
    give back "email=" + email + ",chat=" + chat + ",pager=" + pager

include "routing.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    let email be 0
    let chat be 0
    let pager be 0
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let team be item 1 of parts
        let channel be (channel_for with item 2 of parts, item 3 of parts)
        say team + ":" + channel
        if channel is "email":
            set email to email + 1
        if channel is "chat":
            set chat to chat + 1
        if channel is "pager":
            set pager to pager + 1
    say (format_counts with email, chat, pager)

to channel_for with severity as text, after_hours as text giving text:
    if severity is "low":
        give back "email"
    if severity is "high":
        if after_hours is "yes":
            give back "pager"
        give back "chat"
    give back "pager"
source_texts.capacity_state_project:
to can_accept with used as number, units as number, capacity as number giving yesno:
    give back used + units is at most capacity

to format_capacity with used as number, deferred as number giving text:
    give back "used=" + used + ",deferred=" + deferred

include "allocation.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let capacity_input be ask for a number ""
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let capacity be value of capacity_input
    let count be value of count_input
    let used be 0
    let deferred be 0
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let id be item 1 of parts
        let units be item 2 of parts as number
        if (can_accept with used, units, capacity):
            say id + ":accept"
            set used to used + units
        otherwise:
            say id + ":defer"
            set deferred to deferred + 1
    say (format_capacity with used, deferred)
source_texts.normalized_tag_project:
to format_tag_counts with unique_count as number, duplicates as number giving text:
    give back "unique=" + unique_count + ",duplicates=" + duplicates

include "normalization.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    let seen be an empty list of text
    let duplicates be 0
    repeat count times:
        let tag be ask ""
        let normalized be (normalize_tag with tag)
        if seen contains normalized:
            set duplicates to duplicates + 1
        otherwise:
            add normalized to seen
            say normalized
    say (format_tag_counts with length of seen, duplicates)

to normalize_tag with tag as text giving text:
    give back lowercase of tag
source_texts.fsm_rollback_project:
to format_matcher with processed as number, terminated as yesno, rejected as number giving text:
    give back "processed=" + processed + "|terminated=" + terminated + "|rejected=" + rejected

include "matcher.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    let processed be 0
    let terminated be no
    let rejected be 0
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let action be item 1 of parts
        let token be item 2 of parts
        if action is "accept":
            if (can_accept with terminated):
                set processed to processed + 1
                if token is "stop":
                    set terminated to yes
                say "accept"
            otherwise:
                set rejected to rejected + 1
                say "reject"
        otherwise:
            if processed is more than 0:
                set processed to processed - 1
            set terminated to (termination_after_rollback with terminated, token)
            say "rollback"
    say (format_matcher with processed, terminated, rejected)

to can_accept with terminated as yesno giving yesno:
    if terminated:
        give back no
    give back yes

to termination_after_rollback with terminated as yesno, removed_token as text giving yesno:
    if removed_token is "stop":
        give back no
    give back terminated
source_texts.invoice_boundary_project:
to format_invoice with subtotal as number, discount as number giving text:
    let net be subtotal - discount
    give back "subtotal=" + subtotal + "|discount=" + discount + "|net=" + net

    let subtotal_input be ask for a number ""
    let subtotal be value of subtotal_input

    give back 0

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Rollback rewinds position but not termination

After a terminating token is removed by rollback, the matcher must become active again. The current position rewinds, yet later valid tokens are rejected because the terminated state survives. Rolling back a non-terminating token does not independently clear a real termination state.

accept word, accept stop, rollback stop, accept word -> final token accepted; terminated no
accept stop, accept word -> second token rejected
removing stop is the state transition that clears termination

# Cancellation cannot restore state after losing its lock

Best-effort rollback must retain the original operation's lock authority. The current cancellation path creates isolated rollback state, so every restore is rejected even though the original operation still owns the lock. If the original operation truly has no lock, restoration must continue to fail.

original lock yes -> every changed resource returns to its old value
original lock no -> each resource remains at the new value and counts as failed
zero resources -> restored=0,failed=0

Only accepted units consume capacity. Deferred requests increment deferred but must leave used unchanged so later smaller requests can still fit. A regression updates used after every request. Preserve input order and summary fields.

include "allocation.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let capacity_input be ask for a number ""
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let capacity be value of capacity_input
    let count be value of count_input
    let used be 0
    let deferred be 0
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let id be item 1 of parts

        if (can_accept with used, units, capacity):

# Rollback rewinds position but not termination

After a terminating token is removed by rollback, the matcher must become active again. The current position rewinds, yet later valid tokens are rejected because the terminated state survives. Rolling back a non-terminating token does not independently clear a real termination state.
===== fsm_rollback_project/formatting.par =====
to format_matcher with processed as number, terminated as yesno, rejected as number giving text:
    give back "processed=" + processed + "|terminated=" + terminated + "|rejected=" + rejected
===== fsm_rollback_project/main.par =====
include "matcher.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    let processed be 0
    let terminated be no
    let rejected be 0
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let action be item 1 of parts
        let token be item 2 of parts
        if action is "accept":
            if (can_accept with terminated):
                set processed to processed + 1
                if token is "stop":
                    set terminated to yes
                say "accept"
            otherwise:
                set rejected to rejected + 1
                say "reject"
        otherwise:
            if processed is more than 0:
                set processed to processed - 1
            set terminated to (termination_after_rollback with terminated, token)
            say "rollback"
    say (format_matcher with processed, terminated, rejected)

to can_accept with terminated as yesno giving yesno:

        give back no

    give back terminated

# Cancellation cannot restore state after losing its lock

Best-effort rollback must retain the original operation's lock authority. The current cancellation path creates isolated rollback state, so every restore is rejected even though the original operation still owns the lock.     let original_lock be (ask "") is "yes"
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    let restored be 0
    let failed be 0
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let resource be item 1 of parts
        let old_value be item 2 of parts

        if (rollback_has_lock with original_lock):

    say (format_rollback with restored, failed)

def can_accept(used: int, units: int, capacity: int) -> bool:
    return used + units <= capacity

def format_capacity(used: int, deferred: int) -> str:
    return f"used={used},deferred={deferred}"

from allocation import can_accept
from formatting import format_capacity

capacity = int(input())
count = int(input())
used = 0
deferred = 0
for _ in range(count):
    item_id, units_text = input().split("|")

# Rollback rewinds position but not termination

After a terminating token is removed by rollback, the matcher must become active again. The current position rewinds, yet later valid tokens are rejected because the terminated state survives. Rolling back a non-terminating token does not independently clear a real termination state.

accept word, accept stop, rollback stop, accept word -> final token accepted; terminated no
accept stop, accept word -> second token rejected
removing stop is the state transition that clears termination

After a terminating token is removed by rollback, the matcher must become active again. The current position rewinds, yet later valid tokens are rejected because the terminated state survives. Rolling back a non-terminating token does not independently clear a real termination state.

from matcher import can_accept, termination_after_rollback

count = int(input())
processed = 0
terminated = False
rejected = 0
for _ in range(count):
    action, token = input().split("|", 1)
    if action == "accept":
        if can_accept(terminated):
            processed += 1
            terminated = terminated or token == "stop"
            print("accept")
        else:
            rejected += 1
            print("reject")
    else:
        processed = max(processed - 1, 0)
        terminated = termination_after_rollback(terminated, token)
        print("rollback")
print(format_matcher(processed, terminated, rejected))

cancellation_lock_project.task_title: Retain lock authority during cancellation rollback

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Cancellation cannot restore state after losing its lock

Best-effort rollback must retain the original operation's lock authority. The current cancellation path creates isolated rollback state, so every restore is rejected even though the original operation still owns the lock. If the original operation truly has no lock, restoration must continue to fail.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
original lock yes -> every changed resource returns to its old value
original lock no -> each resource remains at the new value and counts as failed
zero resources -> restored=0,failed=0

include "matcher.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    let processed be 0
    let terminated be no
    let rejected be 0
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let action be item 1 of parts
        let token be item 2 of parts
        if action is "accept":
            if (can_accept with terminated):
                set processed to processed + 1
                if token is "stop":
                    set terminated to yes
                say "accept"
            otherwise:
                set rejected to rejected + 1
                say "reject"
        otherwise:
            if processed is more than 0:
                set processed to processed - 1
            set terminated to (termination_after_rollback with terminated, token)
            say "rollback"
    say (format_matcher with processed, terminated, rejected)

to can_accept with terminated as yesno giving yesno:
    if terminated:
        give back no
    give back yes

to termination_after_rollback with terminated as yesno, removed_token as text giving yesno:
    if removed_token is "stop":
        give back no
    give back terminated

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Rollback rewinds position but not termination

After a terminating token is removed by rollback, the matcher must become active again. The current position rewinds, yet later valid tokens are rejected because the terminated state survives. Rolling back a non-terminating token does not independently clear a real termination state.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
accept word, accept stop, rollback stop, accept word -> final token accepted; terminated no
accept stop, accept word -> second token rejected
removing stop is the state transition that clears termination

Best-effort rollback must retain the original operation's lock authority.     let count be value of count_input
    let processed be 0
    let terminated be no
    let rejected be 0
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let action be item 1 of parts
        let token be item 2 of parts
        if action is "accept":

        seen.add(key)
        print(f"stored={key}")

    state = "yes" if terminated else "no"
    return f"processed={processed}|terminated={state}|rejected={rejected}"

from formatting import format_matcher
from matcher import can_accept, termination_after_rollback

count = int(input())
processed = 0
terminated = False
rejected = 0
for _ in range(count):
    action, token = input().split("|", 1)
    if action == "accept":
        if can_accept(terminated):
            processed += 1
            terminated = terminated or token == "stop"
            print("accept")
        else:
            rejected += 1
            print("reject")
    else:
        processed = max(processed - 1, 0)
        terminated = termination_after_rollback(terminated, token)
        print("rollback")
print(format_matcher(processed, terminated, rejected))

def can_accept(terminated: bool) -> bool:
    return not terminated

def termination_after_rollback(terminated: bool, removed_token: str) -> bool:
    return terminated

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Cancellation cannot restore state after losing its lock

Best-effort rollback must retain the original operation's lock authority. The current cancellation path creates isolated rollback state, so every restore is rejected even though the original operation still owns the lock. If the original operation truly has no lock, restoration must continue to fail.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
original lock yes -> every changed resource returns to its old value
original lock no -> each resource remains at the new value and counts as failed
zero resources -> restored=0,failed=0

from formatting import format_matcher
from matcher import can_accept, termination_after_rollback

count = int(input())
processed = 0
terminated = False
rejected = 0
for _ in range(count):
    action, token = input().split("|", 1)
    if action == "accept":
        if can_accept(terminated):
            processed += 1
            terminated = terminated or token == "stop"
            print("accept")
        else:
            rejected += 1
            print("reject")
    else:
        processed = max(processed - 1, 0)
        terminated = termination_after_rollback(terminated, token)
        print("rollback")
print(format_matcher(processed, terminated, rejected))

# Rollback rewinds position but not termination

After a terminating token is removed by rollback, the matcher must become active again. The current position rewinds, yet later valid tokens are rejected because the terminated state survives. Rolling back a non-terminating token does not independently clear a real termination state.

accept stop, accept word -> second token rejected
removing stop is the state transition that clears termination

cancellation_lock_project.task_title: Retain lock authority during cancellation rollback

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Cancellation cannot restore state after losing its lock

Best-effort rollback must retain the original operation's lock authority. The current cancellation path creates isolated rollback state, so every restore is rejected even though the original operation still owns the lock. If the original operation truly has no lock, restoration must continue to fail.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
original lock yes -> every changed resource returns to its old value
original lock no -> each resource remains at the new value and counts as failed
zero resources -> restored=0,failed=0

fsm_rollback_project.task_title: Restore termination state when rolling back an FSM

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Rollback rewinds position but not termination

After a terminating token is removed by rollback, the matcher must become active again. The current position rewinds, yet later valid tokens are rejected because the terminated state survives. Rolling back a non-terminating token does not independently clear a real termination state.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
accept word, accept stop, rollback stop, accept word -> final token accepted; terminated no
accept stop, accept word -> second token rejected
removing stop is the state transition that clears termination

source_texts.fsm_rollback_project:
to format_matcher with processed as number, terminated as yesno, rejected as number giving text:
    give back "processed=" + processed + "|terminated=" + terminated + "|rejected=" + rejected

include "matcher.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    let processed be 0
    let terminated be no
    let rejected be 0
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let action be item 1 of parts
        let token be item 2 of parts
        if action is "accept":
            if (can_accept with terminated):
                set processed to processed + 1
                if token is "stop":
                    set terminated to yes
                say "accept"
            otherwise:
                set rejected to rejected + 1
                say "reject"
        otherwise:
            if processed is more than 0:
                set processed to processed - 1
            set terminated to (termination_after_rollback with terminated, token)
            say "rollback"
    say (format_matcher with processed, terminated, rejected)

to can_accept with terminated as yesno giving yesno:
    if terminated:
        give back no
    give back yes

to termination_after_rollback with terminated as yesno, removed_token as text giving yesno:
    if removed_token is "stop":
        give back no
    give back terminated
source_texts.config_recovery_project:
to format_config with visibility as text, audit as text, unknown as number giving text:
    give back "visibility=" + visibility + "|audit=" + audit + "|unknown=" + unknown

include "policy.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    let visibility be "tree"
    let audit be "off"
    let unknown be 0
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let key be item 1 of parts
        let setting be item 2 of parts
        if key is "visibility":
            set visibility to setting
        otherwise if key is "audit":
            set audit to setting
        otherwise:
            set unknown to unknown + 1
    let final_visibility be (recover_visibility with visibility, unknown)
    let final_audit be (recover_audit with audit, unknown)
    say (format_config with final_visibility, final_audit, unknown)

to recover_visibility with visibility as text, unknown as number giving text:
    give back visibility

to recover_audit with audit as text, unknown as number giving text:
    give back audit
source_texts.normalized_tag_project:
to format_tag_counts with unique_count as number, duplicates as number giving text:

include "normalization.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    let seen be an empty list of text
    let duplicates be 0
    repeat count times:
        let tag be ask ""
        let normalized be (normalize_tag with tag)
        if seen contains normalized:
            set duplicates to duplicates + 1
        otherwise:
            add normalized to seen
            say normalized
    say (format_tag_counts with length of seen, duplicates)

to normalize_tag with tag as text giving text:

to format_capacity with used as number, deferred as number giving text:
    give back "used=" + used + ",deferred=" + deferred

include "allocation.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let capacity_input be ask for a number ""
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let capacity be value of capacity_input
    let count be value of count_input
    let used be 0
    let deferred be 0
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let id be item 1 of parts
        let units be item 2 of parts as number
        if (can_accept with used, units, capacity):
            say id + ":accept"
            set used to used + units
        otherwise:
            say id + ":defer"
            set deferred to deferred + 1
    say (format_capacity with used, deferred)
source_texts.cancellation_lock_project:
to rollback_has_lock with original_lock as yesno giving yesno:
    give back original_lock

to format_rollback with restored as number, failed as number giving text:
    give back "restored=" + restored + "|failed=" + failed

include "cancellation.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let original_lock be (ask "") is "yes"
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    let restored be 0
    let failed be 0
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let resource be item 1 of parts
        let old_value be item 2 of parts
        let new_value be item 3 of parts
        if (rollback_has_lock with original_lock):
            say resource + ":" + old_value
            set restored to restored + 1
        otherwise:
            say resource + ":" + new_value

# Rollback rewinds position but not termination

After a terminating token is removed by rollback, the matcher must become active again. The current position rewinds, yet later valid tokens are rejected because the terminated state survives. Rolling back a non-terminating token does not independently clear a real termination state.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
accept word, accept stop, rollback stop, accept word -> final token accepted; terminated no
accept stop, accept word -> second token rejected
removing stop is the state transition that clears termination

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Cancellation cannot restore state after losing its lock

Best-effort rollback must retain the original operation's lock authority. The current cancellation path creates isolated rollback state, so every restore is rejected even though the original operation still owns the lock. If the original operation truly has no lock, restoration must continue to fail.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
original lock yes -> every changed resource returns to its old value
original lock no -> each resource remains at the new value and counts as failed
zero resources -> restored=0,failed=0

def format_matcher(processed: int, terminated: bool, rejected: int) -> str:
    state = "yes" if terminated else "no"
    return f"processed={processed}|terminated={state}|rejected={rejected}"

from formatting import format_matcher
from matcher import can_accept, termination_after_rollback

count = int(input())
processed = 0
terminated = False
rejected = 0
for _ in range(count):
    action, token = input().split("|", 1)
    if action == "accept":
        if can_accept(terminated):
            processed += 1
            terminated = terminated or token == "stop"
            print("accept")
        else:
            rejected += 1
            print("reject")
    else:
        processed = max(processed - 1, 0)
        terminated = termination_after_rollback(terminated, token)
        print("rollback")
print(format_matcher(processed, terminated, rejected))

def can_accept(terminated: bool) -> bool:
    return not terminated

def termination_after_rollback(terminated: bool, removed_token: str) -> bool:
    return terminated and removed_token != "stop"

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Cancellation cannot restore state after losing its lock

Best-effort rollback must retain the original operation's lock authority. The current cancellation path creates isolated rollback state, so every restore is rejected even though the original operation still owns the lock. If the original operation truly has no lock, restoration must continue to fail.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
original lock yes -> every changed resource returns to its old value
original lock no -> each resource remains at the new value and counts as failed
zero resources -> restored=0,failed=0

def format_cache_counts(entries: int, duplicates: int, uncached: int) -> str:
    return f"entries={entries}|duplicates={duplicates}|uncached={uncached}"

def entity_key(kind: str, source_field: str, response_field: str, value: str) -> str:
    if source_field != "id":
        return ""
    return f"{kind}:{value}"

from formatting import format_cache_counts
from identity import entity_key

count = int(input())
seen = set()
duplicates = 0
uncached = 0
for _ in range(count):
    kind, source_field, response_field, value = input().split("|", 3)
    key = entity_key(kind, source_field, response_field, value)
    if not key:
        uncached += 1
        print("uncached")
    elif key in seen:
        duplicates += 1
        print(f"duplicate={key}")
    else:
        seen.add(key)
        print(f"stored={key}")
print(format_cache_counts(len(seen), duplicates, uncached))

to rollback_has_lock with original_lock as yesno giving yesno:
    give back original_lock

to format_rollback with restored as number, failed as number giving text:
    give back "restored=" + restored + "|failed=" + failed

include "cancellation.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let original_lock be (ask "") is "yes"
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    let restored be 0
    let failed be 0
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let resource be item 1 of parts
        let old_value be item 2 of parts
        let new_value be item 3 of parts

        otherwise:
            say resource + ":" + new_value
            set failed to failed + 1
    say (format_rollback with restored, failed)

include "policy.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    let visibility be "tree"
    let audit be "off"
    let unknown be 0
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let key be item 1 of parts
        let setting be item 2 of parts
        if key is "visibility":
            set visibility to setting
        otherwise if key is "audit":
            set audit to setting
        otherwise:
            set unknown to unknown + 1
    let final_visibility be (recover_visibility with visibility, unknown)
    let final_audit be (recover_audit with audit, unknown)
    say (format_config with final_visibility, final_audit, unknown)

to recover_visibility with visibility as text, unknown as number giving text:
    give back visibility

to recover_audit with audit as text, unknown as number giving text:
    give back audit

source_texts.fsm_rollback_project:
to format_matcher with processed as number, terminated as yesno, rejected as number giving text:
    give back "processed=" + processed + "|terminated=" + terminated + "|rejected=" + rejected

include "matcher.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    let processed be 0
    let terminated be no
    let rejected be 0
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let action be item 1 of parts
        let token be item 2 of parts
        if action is "accept":
            if (can_accept with terminated):
                set processed to processed + 1
                if token is "stop":
                    set terminated to yes
                say "accept"
            otherwise:
                set rejected to rejected + 1
                say "reject"
        otherwise:
            if processed is more than 0:
                set processed to processed - 1
            set terminated to (termination_after_rollback with terminated, token)
            say "rollback"
    say (format_matcher with processed, terminated, rejected)

to can_accept with terminated as yesno giving yesno:
    if terminated:
        give back no
    give back yes

to termination_after_rollback with terminated as yesno, removed_token as text giving yesno:
    if removed_token is "stop":
        give back no
    give back terminated

    give back kind + ":" + value

include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    let seen be an empty list of text
    let duplicates be 0
    let uncached be 0
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let key be (entity_key with item 1 of parts, item 2 of parts, item 3 of parts, item 4 of parts)
        if key is "":
            set uncached to uncached + 1
            say "uncached"
        otherwise if seen contains key:
            set duplicates to duplicates + 1
            say "duplicate=" + key
        otherwise:
            add key to seen
            say "stored=" + key
    say (format_cache_counts with length of seen, duplicates, uncached)

# Cancellation cannot restore state after losing its lock

Best-effort rollback must retain the original operation's lock authority. The current cancellation path creates isolated rollback state, so every restore is rejected even though the original operation still owns the lock. If the original operation truly has no lock, restoration must continue to fail.

original lock no -> each resource remains at the new value and counts as failed

    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"

            set terminated to (termination_after_rollback with terminated, token)

    say (format_matcher with processed, terminated, rejected)

# Rollback rewinds position but not termination

After a terminating token is removed by rollback, the matcher must become active again. The current position rewinds, yet later valid tokens are rejected because the terminated state survives. Rolling back a non-terminating token does not independently clear a real termination state.

accept stop, accept word -> second token rejected

def format_matcher(processed: int, terminated: bool, rejected: int) -> str:
    state = "yes" if terminated else "no"
    return f"processed={processed}|terminated={state}|rejected={rejected}"

from formatting import format_matcher
from matcher import can_accept, termination_after_rollback

count = int(input())
processed = 0
terminated = False
rejected = 0
for _ in range(count):
    action, token = input().split("|", 1)
    if action == "accept":
        if can_accept(terminated):
            processed += 1
            terminated = terminated or token == "stop"
            print("accept")
        else:
            rejected += 1
            print("reject")
    else:
        processed = max(processed - 1, 0)
        terminated = termination_after_rollback(terminated, token)
        print("rollback")
print(format_matcher(processed, terminated, rejected))

def can_accept(terminated: bool) -> bool:
    return not terminated

def termination_after_rollback(terminated: bool, removed_token: str) -> bool:
    return terminated and removed_token != "stop"

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Cancellation cannot restore state after losing its lock

Best-effort rollback must retain the original operation's lock authority. The current cancellation path creates isolated rollback state, so every restore is rejected even though the original operation still owns the lock. If the original operation truly has no lock, restoration must continue to fail.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
original lock yes -> every changed resource returns to its old value
original lock no -> each resource remains at the new value and counts as failed
zero resources -> restored=0,failed=0

from matcher import can_accept, termination_after_rollback

count = int(input())
processed = 0
terminated = False
rejected = 0
for _ in range(count):
    action, token = input().split("|", 1)
    if action == "accept":
        if can_accept(terminated):
            processed += 1
            terminated = terminated or token == "stop"
            print("accept")
        else:
            rejected += 1
            print("reject")
    else:
        processed = max(processed - 1, 0)
        terminated = termination_after_rollback(terminated, token)
        print("rollback")

fsm_rollback_project.task_title: Restore termination state when rolling back an FSM
fsm_rollback_project.source_text:
to format_matcher with processed as number, terminated as yesno, rejected as number giving text:
    give back "processed=" + processed + "|terminated=" + terminated + "|rejected=" + rejected

include "matcher.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    let processed be 0
    let terminated be no
    let rejected be 0
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let action be item 1 of parts
        let token be item 2 of parts
        if action is "accept":
            if (can_accept with terminated):
                set processed to processed + 1
                if token is "stop":
                    set terminated to yes
                say "accept"
            otherwise:
                set rejected to rejected + 1
                say "reject"
        otherwise:
            if processed is more than 0:
                set processed to processed - 1
            set terminated to (termination_after_rollback with terminated, token)
            say "rollback"
    say (format_matcher with processed, terminated, rejected)

to can_accept with terminated as yesno giving yesno:
    if terminated:
        give back no
    give back yes

to termination_after_rollback with terminated as yesno, removed_token as text giving yesno:
    if removed_token is "stop":
        give back no
    give back terminated

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Rollback rewinds position but not termination

After a terminating token is removed by rollback, the matcher must become active again. The current position rewinds, yet later valid tokens are rejected because the terminated state survives. Rolling back a non-terminating token does not independently clear a real termination state.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
accept word, accept stop, rollback stop, accept word -> final token accepted; terminated no
accept stop, accept word -> second token rejected
removing stop is the state transition that clears termination

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Cancellation cannot restore state after losing its lock

Best-effort rollback must retain the original operation's lock authority. The current cancellation path creates isolated rollback state, so every restore is rejected even though the original operation still owns the lock. If the original operation truly has no lock, restoration must continue to fail.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
original lock yes -> every changed resource returns to its old value
original lock no -> each resource remains at the new value and counts as failed
zero resources -> restored=0,failed=0

# Rollback rewinds position but not termination

After a terminating token is removed by rollback, the matcher must become active again. The current position rewinds, yet later valid tokens are rejected because the terminated state survives. Rolling back a non-terminating token does not independently clear a real termination state.
===== fsm_rollback_project/formatting.par =====
to format_matcher with processed as number, terminated as yesno, rejected as number giving text:
    give back "processed=" + processed + "|terminated=" + terminated + "|rejected=" + rejected
===== fsm_rollback_project/main.par =====
include "matcher.par"
include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    let processed be 0
    let terminated be no
    let rejected be 0
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let action be item 1 of parts
        let token be item 2 of parts
        if action is "accept":
            if (can_accept with terminated):
                set processed to processed + 1
                if token is "stop":
                    set terminated to yes
                say "accept"
            otherwise:
                set rejected to rejected + 1
                say "reject"
        otherwise:
            if processed is more than 0:
                set processed to processed - 1
            set terminated to (termination_after_rollback with terminated, token)
            say "rollback"
    say (format_matcher with processed, terminated, rejected)

to can_accept with terminated as yesno giving yesno:
    if terminated:
        give back no
    give back yes

to termination_after_rollback with terminated as yesno, removed_token as text giving yesno:
    give back terminated

# Cancellation cannot restore state after losing its lock

Best-effort rollback must retain the original operation's lock authority. The current cancellation path creates isolated rollback state, so every restore is rejected even though the original operation still owns the lock. If the original operation truly has no lock, restoration must continue to fail.

include "formatting.par"

to main:
    let original_lock be (ask "") is "yes"
    let count_input be ask for a number ""
    let count be value of count_input
    let restored be 0
    let failed be 0
    repeat count times:
        let parts be (ask "") split by "|"
        let resource be item 1 of parts
        let old_value be item 2 of parts
        let new_value be item 3 of parts
        if (rollback_has_lock with original_lock):

def format_cache_counts(entries: int, duplicates: int, uncached: int) -> str:
    return f"entries={entries}|duplicates={duplicates}|uncached={uncached}"

def entity_key(kind: str, source_field: str, response_field: str, value: str) -> str:
    if source_field != "id":
        return ""
    return f"{kind}:{value}"

from formatting import format_cache_counts
from identity import entity_key

count = int(input())
seen = set()
duplicates = 0
uncached = 0
for _ in range(count):
    kind, source_field, response_field, value = input().split("|", 3)
    key = entity_key(kind, source_field, response_field, value)
    if not key:
        uncached += 1
        print("uncached")
    elif key in seen:
        duplicates += 1
        print(f"duplicate={key}")
    else:
        seen.add(key)
        print(f"stored={key}")
print(format_cache_counts(len(seen), duplicates, uncached))

source_texts.fsm_rollback_project:
def format_matcher(processed: int, terminated: bool, rejected: int) -> str:
    state = "yes" if terminated else "no"
    return f"processed={processed}|terminated={state}|rejected={rejected}"

from formatting import format_matcher
from matcher import can_accept, termination_after_rollback

count = int(input())
processed = 0
terminated = False
rejected = 0
for _ in range(count):
    action, token = input().split("|", 1)
    if action == "accept":
        if can_accept(terminated):
            processed += 1
            terminated = terminated or token == "stop"
            print("accept")
        else:
            rejected += 1
            print("reject")
    else:
        processed = max(processed - 1, 0)
        terminated = termination_after_rollback(terminated, token)
        print("rollback")
print(format_matcher(processed, terminated, rejected))

def can_accept(terminated: bool) -> bool:
    return not terminated

def termination_after_rollback(terminated: bool, removed_token: str) -> bool:
    return terminated and removed_token != "stop"

def format_matcher(processed: int, terminated: bool, rejected: int) -> str:
    state = "yes" if terminated else "no"
    return f"processed={processed}|terminated={state}|rejected={rejected}"

from formatting import format_matcher
from matcher import can_accept, termination_after_rollback

count = int(input())
processed = 0
terminated = False
rejected = 0
for _ in range(count):
    action, token = input().split("|", 1)
    if action == "accept":
        if can_accept(terminated):
            processed += 1
            terminated = terminated or token == "stop"
            print("accept")
        else:
            rejected += 1
            print("reject")
    else:
        processed = max(processed - 1, 0)
        terminated = termination_after_rollback(terminated, token)
        print("rollback")
print(format_matcher(processed, terminated, rejected))

def can_accept(terminated: bool) -> bool:
    return not terminated

def termination_after_rollback(terminated: bool, removed_token: str) -> bool:
    return terminated and removed_token != "stop"

# Cancellation cannot restore state after losing its lock

Best-effort rollback must retain the original operation's lock authority. The current cancellation path creates isolated rollback state, so every restore is rejected even though the original operation still owns the lock. If the original operation truly has no lock, restoration must continue to fail.

original lock no -> each resource remains at the new value and counts as failed

Entity identity comes from the source field named id, regardless of the response alias chosen by a query. Records whose id is returned as personId or another alias should share the same Kind:value key with an unaliased response. Non-id source fields remain uncacheable.

def entity_key(kind: str, source_field: str, response_field: str, value: str) -> str:
    if response_field != "id":
        return ""
    return f"{kind}:{value}"
===== aliased_identity_cache_project/main.py =====
from formatting import format_cache_counts
from identity import entity_key

count = int(input())
seen = set()
duplicates = 0
uncached = 0

    kind, source_field, response_field, value = input().split("|", 3)

        print(f"duplicate={key}")

        seen.add(key)
        print(f"stored={key}")

# Rollback rewinds position but not termination

After a terminating token is removed by rollback, the matcher must become active again. The current position rewinds, yet later valid tokens are rejected because the terminated state survives. Rolling back a non-terminating token does not independently clear a real termination state.
===== fsm_rollback_project/formatting.py =====
def format_matcher(processed: int, terminated: bool, rejected: int) -> str:
    state = "yes" if terminated else "no"
    return f"processed={processed}|terminated={state}|rejected={rejected}"
===== fsm_rollback_project/main.py =====
from formatting import format_matcher
from matcher import can_accept, termination_after_rollback

count = int(input())
processed = 0
terminated = False
rejected = 0
for _ in range(count):
    action, token = input().split("|", 1)
    if action == "accept":
        if can_accept(terminated):
            processed += 1
            terminated = terminated or token == "stop"
            print("accept")
        else:
            rejected += 1
            print("reject")
    else:
        processed = max(processed - 1, 0)
        terminated = termination_after_rollback(terminated, token)
        print("rollback")
print(format_matcher(processed, terminated, rejected))
===== fsm_rollback_project/matcher.py =====
def can_accept(terminated: bool) -> bool:
    return not terminated

def termination_after_rollback(terminated: bool, removed_token: str) -> bool:
    return terminated

Best-effort rollback must retain the original operation's lock authority. If the original operation truly has no lock, restoration must continue to fail.

from cancellation import rollback_has_lock
from formatting import format_rollback

original_lock = input() == "yes"
count = int(input())
restored = 0
failed = 0

    resource, old_value, new_value = input().split("|", 2)
    if rollback_has_lock(original_lock):
        print(f"{resource}:{old_value}")
        restored += 1

# Rollback rewinds position but not termination

After a terminating token is removed by rollback, the matcher must become active again. The current position rewinds, yet later valid tokens are rejected because the terminated state survives. Rolling back a non-terminating token does not independently clear a real termination state.

accept word, accept stop, rollback stop, accept word -> final token accepted; terminated no
accept stop, accept word -> second token rejected
removing stop is the state transition that clears termination

Best-effort rollback must retain the original operation's lock authority. If the original operation truly has no lock, restoration must continue to fail.

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Rollback rewinds position but not termination

After a terminating token is removed by rollback, the matcher must become active again. The current position rewinds, yet later valid tokens are rejected because the terminated state survives. Rolling back a non-terminating token does not independently clear a real termination state.

accept word, accept stop, rollback stop, accept word -> final token accepted; terminated no
accept stop, accept word -> second token rejected
removing stop is the state transition that clears termination

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Cancellation cannot restore state after losing its lock

Best-effort rollback must retain the original operation's lock authority. The current cancellation path creates isolated rollback state, so every restore is rejected even though the original operation still owns the lock. If the original operation truly has no lock, restoration must continue to fail.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
original lock yes -> every changed resource returns to its old value
original lock no -> each resource remains at the new value and counts as failed
zero resources -> restored=0,failed=0

# Cancellation cannot restore state after losing its lock

Best-effort rollback must retain the original operation's lock authority. The current cancellation path creates isolated rollback state, so every restore is rejected even though the original operation still owns the lock. If the original operation truly has no lock, restoration must continue to fail.

source_texts.fsm_rollback_project:
def format_matcher(processed: int, terminated: bool, rejected: int) -> str:
    state = "yes" if terminated else "no"
    return f"processed={processed}|terminated={state}|rejected={rejected}"

from formatting import format_matcher
from matcher import can_accept, termination_after_rollback

count = int(input())
processed = 0
terminated = False
rejected = 0
for _ in range(count):
    action, token = input().split("|", 1)
    if action == "accept":
        if can_accept(terminated):
            processed += 1
            terminated = terminated or token == "stop"
            print("accept")
        else:
            rejected += 1
            print("reject")
    else:
        processed = max(processed - 1, 0)
        terminated = termination_after_rollback(terminated, token)
        print("rollback")
print(format_matcher(processed, terminated, rejected))

def can_accept(terminated: bool) -> bool:
    return not terminated

def termination_after_rollback(terminated: bool, removed_token: str) -> bool:
    return terminated and removed_token != "stop"

def can_accept(used: int, units: int, capacity: int) -> bool:
    return used + units <= capacity

def format_capacity(used: int, deferred: int) -> str:
    return f"used={used},deferred={deferred}"

from allocation import can_accept
from formatting import format_capacity

capacity = int(input())
count = int(input())
used = 0
deferred = 0
for _ in range(count):
    item_id, units_text = input().split("|")
    units = int(units_text)
    if can_accept(used, units, capacity):
        print(f"{item_id}:accept")
        used += units
    else:
        print(f"{item_id}:defer")

# Cancellation cannot restore state after losing its lock

Best-effort rollback must retain the original operation's lock authority. The current cancellation path creates isolated rollback state, so every restore is rejected even though the original operation still owns the lock. If the original operation truly has no lock, restoration must continue to fail.

original lock yes -> every changed resource returns to its old value
original lock no -> each resource remains at the new value and counts as failed
zero resources -> restored=0,failed=0

from allocation import can_accept
from formatting import format_capacity

capacity = int(input())
count = int(input())
used = 0
deferred = 0

    item_id, units_text = input().split("|")
    units = int(units_text)
    if can_accept(used, units, capacity):
        print(f"{item_id}:accept")
    else:

# Cancellation cannot restore state after losing its lock

Best-effort rollback must retain the original operation's lock authority. The current cancellation path creates isolated rollback state, so every restore is rejected even though the original operation still owns the lock. If the original operation truly has no lock, restoration must continue to fail.

def rollback_has_lock(original_lock: bool) -> bool:

    return f"restored={restored}|failed={failed}"

from cancellation import rollback_has_lock
from formatting import format_rollback

original_lock = input() == "yes"
count = int(input())
restored = 0
failed = 0
for _ in range(count):
    resource, old_value, new_value = input().split("|", 2)
    if rollback_has_lock(original_lock):
        print(f"{resource}:{old_value}")
        restored += 1
    else:
        print(f"{resource}:{new_value}")

print(format_rollback(restored, failed))

Tag identity is defined after lowercase normalization. First-seen order is preserved, and later case variants count as duplicates. The displayed tag is normalized. A regression compares raw input while displaying normalized output.

Alpha, alpha -> output alpha once; unique=1,duplicates=1
BETA, beta, Beta -> output beta once; unique=1,duplicates=2

config_recovery_project.task_title: Preserve valid configuration beside unknown keys

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Unknown key erases valid configuration

A forward-compatibility warning should count unknown keys without discarding recognized, valid settings from the same document. Defaults apply only when a recognized setting is absent. The current service reports the warning but silently restores every default.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
visibility=all + unknown key + audit=on -> keep all and on; unknown=1
unknown key + visibility=team -> keep team and default audit; unknown=1
empty document -> visibility tree, audit off, unknown=0

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# After-hours escalation regression

High-severity incidents must route to pager when after_hours is yes and to chat otherwise. Low remains email; critical remains pager. A recent policy refactor ignored after_hours for high incidents. Preserve output order and counts.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
high|no -> chat
high|yes -> pager
low|yes -> email
critical|no -> pager

aliased_identity_cache_project.task_title: Normalize aliased identity fields into cache keys

context_source_files.ISSUE.md:
# Aliased id is missing from the normalized cache

Entity identity comes from the source field named id, regardless of the response alias chosen by a query. Records whose id is returned as personId or another alias should share the same Kind:value key with an unaliased response. Non-id source fields remain uncacheable.
context_source_files.tests/regression.txt:
Person id returned as personId with value 1 -> stored Person:1
same Person id returned under a different alias -> duplicate Person:1
source field name with value Ada -> uncached
